title: Three Weeks and One Short Tray
subtitle: 健康医疗 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 健康医疗（人与自我·生活与学习·健康的生活方式、个人安全与自救）
meta: 主题语境：健康医疗（人与自我·生活与学习·健康的生活方式、个人安全与自救）　|　核心词汇：supplement　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 supplement 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1969 the baker ① added the supplement that no customer in the bakery would have measured, and he said the adding was the whole of the week. The ② supplement, meaning the addition itself and not the tray, ran three weeks and stayed unmeasured in the book; a supplement, he said, is the only thing in a bakery that is judged by how long it is left unmeasured.

Every ③ supplement in that bakery had the same short tray beside it, and the ④ supplement at the far oven, meaning the slice they kept for the children to taste and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A supplement, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to measure; the baker said the measuring is the part that fills three weeks.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the supplement was the whole of the matter, meaning the care and not the addition. The ⑥ supplement, meaning the care and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody measures; supplement, he said, is either something you add or the only word that means both an addition and a care. He said the care is the part they remember.

By 1974 the ⑦ supplement had become a line in a bill, and the bill had become an argument about the short tray. The ⑧ supplement of the whole thing, the baker wrote in December, was one bakery and three weeks of measuring; supplement, he said, is either the slice at the far oven or the reason you learned to measure. He said the measuring was never mentioned.

The ⑨ supplement I remember is the addition measured in the bill, which closed in 1976 and is still measured as the quietest in the bakery. A ⑩ supplement, my mother said in 1978, is the only addition that improves by being measured; every supplement, she said, is a care that has agreed to look like an addition. She said the care was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 补充；增刊（指糕饼铺里每一份旁边的那一份）
B. n. 补充；增刊（指那份补充本身，与薄薄的托盘相对）
C. 固定搭配：add the supplement 添这一份补充
D. n. 补充；增刊（指留给孩子们尝的那一片）
E. n. 补充之事（抽象总称，指一处糕饼铺的补充之事）
F. n. 补充；增刊（指账单里写到、被测量的那一份）
G. n. 补充、补益（指一件事里人人都尝却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 补益（抽象总称，指人人都尝却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: added the supplement that no customer in the bakery would have measured
The supplement, meaning the addition itself and not the tray
the supplement at the far oven
the supplement was the whole of the matter
the supplement had become a line in a bill
The supplement of the whole thing
A supplement, my mother said in 1978

answers.why: add the supplement 意为“添这一份补充”，1969 年那位面点师把糕饼铺里没有一位顾客肯测量的一份补充做了一遍。
supplement 意为“补充；增刊”，指那份补充本身而不是薄薄的托盘，它经过了三个星期而在簿子上没有被测量。
supplement 意为“补充；增刊”，指糕饼铺里每一份旁边的那一份，每一份旁边都有同一只薄薄的托盘。
supplement 意为“补充；增刊”，指最远那座炉口的留给孩子们尝的那一片，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
supplement 意为“补充、补益”，指一件事里人人都尝却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这份补益就是那件事的全部。
supplement 意为“补益”，指人人都尝却无人提起的那样东西而不是那份补充，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
supplement 意为“补充；增刊”，指账单里写到、被测量的那一份，到 1974 年这一份成了账单里的一行。
supplement 意为“补充之事”，面点师十二月写道，整件事的补充之事是一处糕饼铺和三个星期的测量。
supplement 意为“补充；增刊”，我记得的是账单里测量过的那一份，1976 年卖完了，至今仍被说成糕饼铺里最安静的一份。
supplement 为抽象总称，母亲 1978 年说，补充是唯一会因为被好好测量而变得更好的补充。
